notes:
Summary: BridgePoint builds real-time personalization widgets for high-traffic e‑commerce sites (product recommendations, checkout upsell). Extremely latency-sensitive: client-side rendering budget ~60ms; server round-trip target p95 <40ms for small chat/rerank requests. Cost-sensitive at scale — 200M monthly inference tokens during peak. Interested in Redwood primarily for predictable latency and batching/caching knobs to control unit economics.

What they told us: "We will trade a few points of quality if it drops qps cost by 30% and gives reliable p99 spikes mitigation." CTO (Samir Rao). Prefer open model variants (Llama/Eleuther/Redwood-curated) with quantization options. Strong preference for VPC deployment (dedicated) for PCI adjacency, but will pilot hosted if latency SLOs can be demonstrated.

Technical asks: perf benchmark harness for 1) micro-batched chat (batch sizes 1-8), 2) embedding throughput with prefix caching, 3) quantized fp16/int8 model comparison (latency and token cost). Want p99, p95, median latencies and cost per 1M tokens. Also request tooling or scripts to reproduce in-house.

POC milestones (agreed):
- Week 0: share sample traffic trace + prompt templates (done: uploaded).
- Week 1: Redwood runs synthetic perf harness (1 qps -> 200 qps), returns CSV + dashboards (pending).
- Week 2: KV/prefix cache test with 10k warm keys and 99% hit simulated.
- Week 3: Quantization trade-off report (FP16 vs INT8) with quality comparison on 200 prompt set.
- Week 4: Canary on staging (10 qps live traffic for 48 hours).

Recent timeline / activity log:
- 2026-01-28: Intro call (AE Sophie) — high-level requirements, sent NDA.
- 2026-02-03: Tech deep-dive (SE Arjun) — discussed batching strategies, cache TTLs, routing policies; noted need for on-prem comparison. (gm-thread-20260203-bridgepoint-eval)
- 2026-02-12: Executive demo + perf ask — recorded (ff_20260212_bridgepoint_eval).
- 2026-02-18: Security questionnaire submitted; legal flagged SLA language around data residency. (drive://redwood/security/bridgepoint-security-answers.md)

Sales notes / negotiation stance: procurement wants a firm cap on 99th percentile latency and credits if breached; finance is focused on committed reserved capacity pricing vs pay-as-you-go. They are willing to commit to Dedicated if we can show 25-40% cost reduction via batching + caching + INT8 quantization without >3% quality delta on rerank metric.

Open items / asks for Redwood:
- Provide reproducible perf harness + scripts (Docker + small k8s job) for their infra team.
- Example configs of batching windows and autoscale policies for 10-500 qps.
- Quantization notes: expected latency uplift and recommended fallback policies when quantized model fails checks.
- Security/legal: template residency clause and SOC2 evidence.

Stubs/refs: pricing deck link (drive://redwood/decks/bridgepoint-pricing-v2.pdf), Jira tickets created for perf run (RED-3421) and security answers follow up (RED-3498).
summary: BridgePoint is evaluating Redwood for latency-critical personalization. Primary drivers: p99/p95 latency guarantees, unit-cost reduction via batching/caching/quantization, and VPC-ready deployment. Evaluation POC focused on reproducible perf benchmarks and security checklist.
